data.why: Neuroglancer is purely client-side and loads volumetric data directly from a remote HTTP store; the repo's own docs/gallery/index.rst links the public google/neuroglancer-public-data GCS bucket (flyem_fib-25 EM + segmentation) as example data, so the browser fetches it live instead of anything being bundled or uploaded.

goals: Load a precomputed EM image volume and its matching segmentation layer to inspect cell ultrastructure and cell boundaries side by side
Navigate orthogonal cross-sectional planes (XY, XZ, YZ) and the 3-D view together to understand a neuron's 3-D shape from 2-D sections
Select one or more segmented objects (neurons) by clicking in the segmentation layer and view their reconstructed 3-D meshes
Adjust layer opacity and toggle layer visibility to compare raw EM signal against the segmentation overlay
Pan, zoom, and reorient the view (shift+drag, arrow keys) to trace a process (axon/dendrite) across sections
Inspect rendering/shader and coordinate-space settings for an image layer to understand how voxel data maps to physical units

review.summary: This is a well-structured Neuroglancer tree. Its phases follow how a scientist works through an EM-plus-segmentation dataset, its general labels are clean, its features are sensibly cut, and 10 of the 11 sampled screens match their nodes. It needs a few fixes before filing: one overstated screenshot claim, a wrong feature-to-task mapping, the unsupported 'proofreading' framing, and the missing README essentials of loading your own data and oblique sections.
